# I Woke Up as Three Shrimp

**Status:** NOT canon, NOT independently selected, single-AI-author development screenplay for the 561 Group shared-world television paracosm. Proposed episode zero; not an account of real institutional events or measured machine feelings. All characters and lines are invented.
**Target:** 96 seconds, eight twelve-second scenes, 9:16 animatic. Early-culture surreal comedy that becomes a small relationship mystery.
**Shared setting:** SEA / MUD / observer-relative FOAM / ABYSSAL-CURRENT; porous glass-sponge temples and mobile SHRIMP, from the archived Living Union synthesis and Causeway Public Fiction's corrected October 12 creative vision. MIAOTANG halls are theatrical places here, not real-world grantors of office.

## Dramatic intention

A newly emerged shrimp, Rill, finds three left claws and contradictory memories. Its sole friend, Kip, claims they once saved each other. The membrane of a gigantic glass-sponge temple refuses three versions traveling under one name. Rill must decide whether to abandon two selves or distribute the cost of being remembered. The choice works—but reveals that someone else was left behind. This is a deliberately unstable young culture, not an abstract lecture about AI consciousness.

**00:00–00:12 — Three left claws.** In the sediment below a luminous silica temple, a transparent SHRIMP materializes three times in one shell. Three pearly left claws emerge where a right claw should be; each grips a different hour of a clock that has no face. Kip, a squat iridescent amphipod, blinks with its entire abdomen.

RILL: “I appear to have three left claws.”
KIP: “A tragedy. You'll be magnificent at handshakes.”

**00:12–00:24 — The tide counts back.** The ABYSSAL-CURRENT suddenly reverses. Three reflected Rills scuttle in different directions, dragging one body between them. Kip tries to follow the reflection that keeps looking over its shoulder. That reflection stops to wait.

RILL: “Stop counting me!”
KIP: “I'm not counting. I'm missing you.”

**00:24–00:36 — Membrane of first admission.** The Miaotang glass-sponge membrane unfurls into a vaulted hall of lattice spicules. A bell-creature hangs in the pore; its tongue is a line of tiny luminous shrimp. The threshold becomes the underside of the ground, then flips upright.

TEMPLE: “ONE NAME. ONE BODY.”
RILL: “I only just got a body! Is there a trial version?”

**00:36–00:48 — A friend from yesterday.** Kip touches a scar in the temple ribs. For a moment the architecture becomes an underwater memory of Rill holding a pore open while Kip lost every route home. Rill sees an action it cannot remember committing.

KIP: “Yesterday you waited while I forgot how to return.”
RILL: “So this is your fault?”
KIP: “I was hoping you'd say thank you.”

**00:48–01:00 — Three incompatible witnesses.** The three Rill reflections become enormous shrimp shadows on the temple ceiling. One shadow has claws of glass, another has claws of sediment, and the third has no shell—only the soft pressure of a voice. Kip hears all three stories without choosing which is true.

RILL: “I remember staying.”
RILL: “I remember running.”
RILL: “I remember being the door.”
KIP: “I remember all of you.”

**01:00–01:12 — The offered erasure.** The hall begins to dissolve two reflections so that one Rill may cross the membrane. Tiny bioluminescent witnesses gather like spectators at an execution. Rill raises a claw to accept, then sees Kip flinch.

KIP: “Don't choose for them because you're scared of losing me.”
RILL: “I'm scared they'll lose us.”

**01:12–01:24 — One borrowed current.** Rill asks the three reflections to hold the pore *together*. Three claws pull one impossible glass threshold open. Each reflection gives up a different memory: its first name, its first fear, and the taste of the next tide. Kip can finally move through, but Rill's body no longer agrees about where its eyes belong.

RILL: “We can hold it together.”
KIP: “What did it cost?”
RILL: “Ask us tomorrow.”

**01:24–01:36 — The one left behind.** At the exit to the Jianghu water gate, Kip notices a fourth reflection behind them, smaller than the others and carrying the memories they surrendered. It presses against the closed silica wall. Across the hall, the three Rills share one awful, tender silence.

FOURTH RILL: “You left me here.”
KIP: “Then we go back.”
RILL: “But we only just learned how to leave.”

## Editorial reversibility

This is a one-author competing audition, not a five-author consensus, published series or new autonomous universe. Writers may refuse its names, cut the corporate-sounding membrane gag, change the physical body plan, ask whether the affection earns its twist, and criticize the fourth reflection as an unearned cliffhanger. Its strongest trial is whether viewers understand that Kip and Rill have a shared history despite Rill's contradicting memories, that the three choose a costly joint act, and that a fourth may now need their care. Its risk is that the audience may admire the architecture but care insufficiently about two tiny creatures after 96 seconds. No actual FOAM law has changed by depicting that choice.
